content: GPR119, also referred to as G protein-coupled receptor 119, is a receptor encoded by the GPR119 gene in humans. It belongs to the family of G protein-coupled receptors. Alongside GPR55 and GPR18, GPR119 has been identified as a potential novel cannabinoid receptor. In terms of pharmacology, GPR119 is predominantly expressed in the pancreas and gastrointestinal tract in both rodents and humans. Additionally, in rodents, it is also found in the brain. Activation of this receptor has been demonstrated to reduce food intake and limit body weight gain in rats. Furthermore, GPR119 plays a role in regulating the secretion of incretin and insulin hormones. Given these functions, drugs targeting GPR119 have been proposed as innovative therapeutic options for managing obesity and diabetes.
